sub_unit_name: Conducting polymers: Characteristics and Classification with examples-mechanism of conduction in trans-polyacetylene and applications of conducting polymers

content.title: Conducting Polymers
content.description: Conducting polymers are organic polymers that possess electrical conductivity due to the presence of conjugated double bonds in their molecular structure. Their conductivity can be greatly increased by the process of doping.

content.content: Unlike conventional polymers, conducting polymers can conduct electricity because of the movement of π-electrons along the polymer backbone. These materials combine the flexibility and light weight of plastics with the electrical properties of metals and semiconductors.

content.title: Engineering Importance
content.content: Conducting polymers are used in rechargeable batteries, solar cells, sensors, LEDs, anti-static coatings, flexible electronics, and electromagnetic shielding.

items.question: Electrical Conductivity
items.answer: Conduct electricity due to delocalized π-electrons.

items.question: Flexible
items.answer: Can be processed into thin films and flexible devices.

items.question: Corrosion Resistant
items.answer: Offer better resistance to corrosion than many metals.

items.question: Dopable
items.answer: Electrical conductivity increases significantly after doping.

content.content: Conducting polymers are broadly classified into intrinsically conducting polymers and extrinsically conducting polymers. Intrinsic polymers conduct due to conjugated double bonds, whereas extrinsic polymers become conducting by adding conducting fillers such as carbon black or metal particles.

rows: Conduct by addition of conducting fillers

content.content: Trans-polyacetylene is the first widely studied conducting polymer. It contains alternating single and double bonds, producing a conjugated system that allows π-electrons to move along the polymer chain.

In trans-polyacetylene, the alternating single and double bonds create delocalized π-electrons. During doping with oxidizing or reducing agents, additional charge carriers (electrons or holes) are generated. These charge carriers move freely along the conjugated polymer chain, resulting in high electrical conductivity.

items.question: Rechargeable Batteries
items.answer: Used as electrode materials because of good electrical conductivity.

items.question: Solar Cells
items.answer: Used in lightweight and flexible photovoltaic devices.

items.question: Sensors
items.answer: Applied in chemical, gas, and biosensors.

items.question: Anti-static Coatings
items.answer: Prevent the accumulation of static electricity.

items.question: Flexible Electronics
items.answer: Used in wearable electronics, OLEDs, and smart displays.

content.title: Exam Tip
content.content: Remember the classification, characteristics, conduction mechanism in trans-polyacetylene, and applications of conducting polymers. Questions on doping are frequently asked.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Conducting polymers contain conjugated double bonds.
They are classified as intrinsic and extrinsic conducting polymers.
Doping creates charge carriers responsible for conduction.
They are used in batteries, sensors, LEDs, solar cells, and anti-static coatings.
Conducting polymers combine flexibility with electrical conductivity.
